new_entities.name: Intensive glycaemic control
new_entities.description: Intensive glycaemic control as a behavioral exposure or management strategy.

new_entities.name: Diabetic retinopathy
new_entities.description: Retinal microvascular disease associated with diabetes, including progression outcomes.

edges.effect_quant: Across randomized-trial meta-analyses in type 2 diabetes, intensive glycaemic control consistently lowers retinopathy progression risk, though the effect is modest rather than dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Lower long-term glucose exposure reduces retinal microvascular injury, oxidative stress, and glycation-driven damage to capillaries and neural retinal tissue. The benefit shows up most clearly in slowing progression rather than in completely preventing every retinal complication.
edges.summary: This is a solid microvascular-protection edge. Multiple meta-analyses of randomized trials show that tighter glycaemic control reduces retinopathy progression and related ocular interventions, even though the magnitude is not large enough to erase retinopathy risk altogether.
edges.caveats: The benefit has to be balanced against hypoglycaemia risk and is not a free pass to intensify glucose lowering in every patient. Most of the evidence is about progression-related outcomes in established type 2 diabetes rather than universal primary prevention.

evidence.citation: Kunutsor SK et al 2024 Diabetes Obes Metab
evidence.notes: Glycaemic control and macrovascular and microvascular outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis of trials investigating intensive glucose-lowering strategies in people with type 2 diabetes.
